recipe.notes: The library's defaults when its client is built without LLM, embedder or reranker clients: OpenAIClient (llm_client/openai_base_client.py DEFAULT_MODEL='gpt-5.5', DEFAULT_SMALL_MODEL='gpt-4.1-nano'; reasoning 'auto' resolves to effort 'none' for gpt-5.5), OpenAIEmbedder (embedder/openai.py DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL='text-embedding-3-small'; embedder/client.py EMBEDDING_DIM env default 1024, applied by truncating the returned vector), OpenAIRerankerClient (cross_encoder/openai_reranker_client.py DEFAULT_MODEL='gpt-4.1-nano', one logprob-scored chat call per candidate passage). The shim passes these same values explicitly so the record and the run cannot drift.

common.notes: Both LLM roles (main and small) are set to gpt-4.1-mini. Dimensions are set the way the library sets them: OpenAIEmbedderConfig.embedding_dim truncates the 3,072-dimension text-embedding-3-large vector client-side (the API's `dimensions` parameter is never sent). The reranker is outside the common contract and stays at the recipe's gpt-4.1-nano.

capabilities.time_notes: add_episode(reference_time=session event_time). In message granularity each turn gets reference_time = event_time + turn_index milliseconds so retrieve_episodes (ORDER BY valid_at DESC) sees the conversation order instead of ties. search_ takes no query time, so query_time is ignored and applied_settings says so. An event_time or query_time without a UTC offset is read as UTC.
capabilities.granularity: session (default, SHIM_GRANULARITY=session): one EpisodeType.message episode per session whose body is the session's 'speaker: text' lines. message (SHIM_GRANULARITY=message): one episode per turn, as the vendor's LoCoMo harness does. The metered smoke measures both; the preregistration fixes one.

provenance.mechanism: Mixed by item class. Edges (facts): EntityEdge.episodes lists the episodes that produced or re-asserted the fact; episode uuids map to source ids through the episode name (source_id or source_id#turn) via EpisodicNode.get_by_uuids, provenance exact (partial if an episode was deleted). Entity nodes: EntityNode carries no episodes field at the pinned release (nodes.py:499-504); the public classmethod EpisodicNode.get_by_entity_node_uuid returns the episodes with a MENTIONS edge to the node, reported as partial because the node summary is rewritten per episode and need not reflect every mention. Set settings.node_provenance='none' to report entity nodes as unavailable. Episodes: exact (the episode itself). Communities: unavailable (none are built).

capabilities.delete_notes: The library's remove_episode for every episode of the source (its client module, lines 1824-1855). Its semantics are the product's: it deletes edges whose FIRST episode is the removed one (even if later episodes re-asserted them), keeps edges first created by another episode (their episodes list keeps the removed uuid), and deletes entity nodes mentioned only by the removed episode. P2 measures the residue; the shim does not repair it.
capabilities.readiness: synchronous: add_episode returns after extraction, resolution and writes; /finish has no background work to wait for
capabilities.namespace: group_id (group_id = ns, one Neo4j database); reset = graph_data_operations.clear_data(driver, group_ids=[ns])

vendor-default.notes: The library's search_() with no config argument: COMBINED_HYBRID_SEARCH_CROSS_ENCODER (edges, nodes, episodes and communities; BM25 + cosine + BFS candidates, cross-encoder rerank) at SearchConfig's default limit 10 per class (search_config.py DEFAULT_SEARCH_LIMIT).

fixed-evidence.notes: The same recipe with 50 results per class, enough to fill the 8,000-token evidence budget (facts run about 25 tokens, node summaries about 100); the harness packer truncates.

allowed_settings_overrides: recipe (any upper-case name in the library's search.search_config_recipes module)

vendor_benchmark_reference.notes: The vendor's LoCoMo harness (its search script) runs these two searches against the hosted service and renders facts as '<fact> (event_time: <valid_at>)' followed by entities as '<name>: <summary>'. Recorded for reference, not a shootout policy.

retrieval_policies.item_mapping: search_ returns separate ranked lists per class whose reranker scores are not on one scale, so the shim concatenates them in a fixed class order, each in temporal-graph's own rank order: edges, then entity nodes, then episodes, then communities (the vendor's harness also puts facts before entities). Edge -> type fact, text = fact, valid_from = valid_at, valid_to = invalid_at. Node -> type entity, text = '<name>: <summary>'. Episode -> type episode, text = content, valid_from = valid_at. Community -> type observation, text = '<name>: <summary>'. Raw per-class uuids and reranker scores are returned under raw.

agent_surface.version: see comparison-systems table: temporal-graph (the vendor's MCP server at commit 11538f6d45561bcce9a4400b374fb2dc533dccb6); its pyproject accepts library releases newer than the pin, so the Cat 40 build must constrain the library to the pinned release

deviations_from_vendor_code: The hosted service's graph.add(data, type='message', created_at, group_id) becomes the library's add_episode(episode_body, source=EpisodeType.message, reference_time, group_id); the hosted service is a different product built on temporal-graph.

Default granularity is one episode per session, not the vendor harness's one per message: per-message ingestion multiplies extraction calls by the turns per session (about 30x on LoCoMo) and, with every turn carrying the session time, makes temporal-graph's previous-episode window pick tied episodes in arbitrary order. SHIM_GRANULARITY=message reproduces the vendor harness's granularity, with millisecond offsets that keep turn order.

Episode body lines are 'speaker: content' exactly as the harness sends each turn; the vendor harness appended '(description of attached image: <blip_caption>)' itself, here any caption arrives inside content.
source_description='chat conversation' (the library requires one and shows it to the extraction prompt; the hosted service's add has no such field).
Episode name = opaque source_id (or source_id#turn) so provenance and deletion map back to sessions through public node APIs; names are not shown to any prompt.
group_id = opaque namespace id instead of 'locomo_experiment_user_<idx>'.

Retrieval follows the shootout's two policies over the library's search_() rather than the vendor harness's two-search recipe, which is recorded under vendor_benchmark_reference; the edge validity window travels in valid_from/valid_to instead of being printed into the text.

Provider clients are constructed explicitly with the configured models and OPENAI_BASE_URL rather than relying on temporal-graph()'s implicit defaults; for SHIM_CONFIG=recipe the values are identical.
